Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:1.hebrew: משתמש בהן בחמין - וכ"ש בצונן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:1.english: He uses them with hot [water] - And all the more so with cold [water].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:2.hebrew: אבל לא ע"י האור - לא יתן הכלי על האור:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:2.english: But not by means of the fire - He should not place the vessel on the fire.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:3.hebrew: מגריפות - וודיל"ש, עשויין לגרוף הכירות או להפריש תאנים המדובקים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:3.english: Shovels - Vediles [in Old French], [which are] made for raking out stoves or for separating figs that are stuck together.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:12:4.english: That it diminishes them - It notches them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:13:1.hebrew: מאי עבידתיה גביה - מה לו להשתמש בו? יבא בעליו וישתמש בו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:13:1.english: What is its business with him - What [business] does he have to use it? Let its owner come and use it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:14:1.english: And disregard them - And it comes to teach you that it is permitted to disregard [them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:14:2.english: And [there are] occasions [in] which you may not disregard - As it is written: "You may not disregard [them]" [Deuteronomy 22:3].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:15:1.english: And it is in the graveyard - The lost item is in the graveyard.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:15:2.english: And it is not in keeping with his dignity - That he should return it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:15:3.english: Or that he was idle from his own work - [Meaning] that [what] he would lose by returning it is greater than the value of the lost item.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:16:1.hebrew: האי עשה - השב תשיבם. ואע"ג דלא תעשה נמי איכא, אין לא תעשה מועיל לדחות לא תעשה, אלא עשה הוא דקא דחי ליה, כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף כא.):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:16:1.english: This [is] a positive commandment - "You shall surely return them" [Deuteronomy 22:1]. And even though there is also a negative commandment, a negative commandment does not avail to override a negative commandment; rather, it is the positive commandment that overrides it, as we say in Yevamot (21a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:16:2.hebrew: לא תעשה ועשה - לנפש לא יטמא, קדושים יהיו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:16:2.english: A prohibition and a positive commandment - "For a [dead] person he shall not defile himself" [Leviticus 21:1], [and] "They shall be holy" [Leviticus 21:6].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:1:1.hebrew: בתורי - בפועלים המנהיגים בשוורי בעה"ב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:1:1.english: With oxen - [With] laborers who lead the owner's oxen.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:1:2.hebrew: דנפיש פסידייהו - שרוב עבודת קרקעות שלהן בשוורים היתה; אף חרישת הכרמים ובצירתם — מנהיגים כלי המחרישה בעגלה בין שורות הכרם עם הבוצרים, ונותנין שם הענבים. לפיכך, אם אין הבעלים עליהם, יש הפסד גדול, שאין דרך הפועלים לחוס על הכרם ועל השוורים, ומנהיגים אותן על הגפנים ועל הנטיעות, והם מתקלקלין, והשוורין נסחבין ונשברים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:1:2.english: Whose damage is great - For most of their agricultural work was [done] with oxen; even [during] the plowing of the vineyards and their grape-harvesting, they drive the plowing implements in a wagon between the rows of the vineyard alongside the harvesters, and place the grapes there. Therefore, if the owners are not [watching] over them, there is great loss, for it is not the way of laborers to spare the vineyard or the oxen, and they drive them over the vines and over the saplings, and they [the vines and saplings] are ruined, and the oxen are dragged and injured.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:4:1.english: A hanger [magod] - Kevilla in Old French [i.e., cheville, a peg].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:4:2.hebrew: נזדמנו לו אורחים - קס"ד טעמא משום דמתכבד בהם, ואיכא לצורכה ולצרכו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:4:2.english: Guests happened [to visit] him - It was initially assumed [that] the reason is because he gains honor through them, and there is [thus both] for its sake and for his sake.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:5:1.hebrew: שאני התם דקא קלי לה - בשטיחה זו הוא שורפה, ומה הוא שריפתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:5:1.english: It is different there, as he is burning it - By this spreading, he burns it; and what is its burning?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:5:2.english: Either due to [the] eye - That the evil eye of guests will have power over it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:5:3.english: Or due to thieves - Lest the guests steal it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:6:1.hebrew: הכניסה לרבקה - בעגלה ערופה קאי. רבקה - קופל"ה בלע"ז, שמדבקים שלש בהמות או ארבעה בצואריהן זו אצל זו, ודשים הדישה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:6:1.english: He brought it into a rivkah - [This] refers to the decapitated calf [eglah arufah]. Rivkah — cople in Old French [a coupling/yoke], where they join three or four animals together by their necks, and they perform the threshing.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:6:2.english: [It is] fit - Since he did not intend for it to thresh.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:6:3.hebrew: ואם בשביל שתינק ותידוש - שהיתה אמה דשה, והכניס את הבת לשם שתינק, ואף נתכוין שתדוש, פסולה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:6:3.english: And if [it was] so that it will suckle and thresh - For its mother was threshing, and he brought the daughter [calf] in so that it would suckle, and he also intended that it should thresh — it is unfit.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:9:1.english: This is not comparable - It is an answer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:9:2.english: A bird rested upon it - [This] refers to a red heifer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:9:3.hebrew: עלה עליה זכר פסולה - שנאמר אשר לא עלה עליה עול, ותניא: עול אין לי אלא עול כו' במסכת סוטה (דף מו.). והאי הכניסה לרבקה ודשה דלא ניחא ליה בה, דמיא לשכן עליה עוף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 30a:9:3.english: If a male mounted it, it is unfit - As it is stated: "upon which no yoke has come" [Numbers 19:2], and it was taught [in a baraita]: "[From the word] 'yoke,' I have [derived] only a yoke, etc." in Tractate Sotah (46a). And this [case of] bringing it into a threshing team and it threshed, where he is not pleased with it, is comparable to "a bird rested upon it."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:11:1.hebrew: אף עובד דניחא ליה - וא"ת: ובפרה אדומה מנלן דבעינן דניחא ליה? דבשלמא למאן דיליף (סוטה דף מו.) עבודות בפרה מג"ש ד"עול עול" — ניחא; אלא למאן דלית ליה ג"ש ומשכח עבודות בפרה גופיה, מנלן דבעינן דניחא ליה? וי"ל: דכיון דשוין בפסול עול ועבודות, גם לענין דניחא ליה יש להשוותן. וא"ת: ועלה עליה זכר אמאי פסולה? הא ודאי לא ניחא ליה להפסיל פרה שדמיה יקרים בשביל דבר מועט! וי"ל: דאם היתה כשירה הוה ניחא ליה, ולכך אין להכשיר. וא"ת: הכניסה לרבקה ודשה אמאי כשירה? מאי שנא מעלה עליה זכר דפסולה? וי"ל: דהתם לא ניחא ליה בדישתה, שאינו מרויח כ"כ, דבלאו הכי נדושת התבואה. וא"ת: אי לא ידע בשעת עליית הזכר אמאי פסולה? מאי שנא מהכשר, דאמרינן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף כב.): "נגבו — אינן בכי יותן"? ואם נאמר דלא מיפסלא אלא כשידע בשעת עלייתו — א"ש. ואתי נמי שפיר הא דתנן (פרה פ"ב מ"א): "פרה מעוברת — ר"א מכשיר", וקשה: וכי לית ליה "עלה עליה זכר פסולה"? ולמאי דפרישית אתי שפיר! אי נמי סבר כר"י, דאמר דוקא העלה עליה זכר, אבל עלה מאיליו — כשירה. וה"ר יצחק מסימפון פירש: דלא פליגי בפרה עצמה אלא בבתה; וטעמא דרבנן דפסולה — כדדרשינן בספרי: "ויקחו אליך פרה" — בעינן שתהא בשעת לקיחה פרה, ור"א לית ליה ההיא דרשה. וה"ה דמצו פליגי בלקחו פרה קטנה. וא"ת: העושה מלאכה בפרת חטאת, דאמר בפ' הכונס (ב"ק דף נו. ושם) דחייב בדיני שמים — אמאי מיפסלא? הא ודאי לא ניחא להו לבעלים! וי"ל: כגון שהיה שותף; אי נמי: לא בעינן ניחותא דבעלים, רק ניחותא דעושה מלאכה. וא"ת: בפרק אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כג:), דפוסל ר"א פרה הניקחת מן הנכרים דחייש לרביעה, ודייק: ש"מ קדשי מזבח היא, דאי קדשי בדק הבית היא אמאי פסולה משום רביעה? לימא דפסולה משום עול! וי"ל: דמשמע ליה דלאו מטעם עול פוסל, דקתני בסיפא "וכן היה ר"א פוסל בשאר קרבנות"; לכך קאמר דקדשי מזבח היא, דממעטינן נרבע מקרא ד"מן הבהמה": [וע"ע תוס' ע"ז כג: ד"ה ש"מ]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:11:1.english: "So too, ubbad [means] that [the owner] is amenable to it" - And if you ask: With regard to the red heifer, from where do we [derive] that we require that [the owner] is amenable to it? For it is well according to the one who derives (Sotah 46a) [disqualification through] labors in [the case of] the red heifer from the verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] of "yoke, yoke"; however, according to the one who does not hold of [that] gezeirah shavah and finds [the disqualification of] labors in [the verses of] the red heifer itself, from where do we [derive] that we require that [the owner] is amenable to it? And one can say: Since they are equal regarding the disqualification of a yoke and labors, with respect to [requiring] that [the owner] is amenable to it as well, we should equate them. And if you ask: If a male mounted it, why is it disqualified? Surely [the owner] is certainly not amenable to disqualifying a cow whose value is expensive for a small matter! And one can say: If it were [still] fit, he would be amenable to it, and therefore one should not declare it fit. And if you ask: If he brought it into the stall [rivkah] and it threshed, why is it fit? How is this different from [when] a male mounted it, where it is disqualified? And one can say: There, he is not amenable to its threshing, because he does not profit so much, since the grain would be threshed anyway. And if you ask: If he did not know at the time of the male's mounting, why is it disqualified? How is this different from [the law of] susceptibility to impurity [hekhsher], where we say above (Bava Metzia 22a): "If they dried off, they are not [subject to] 'when [water] is placed'"? And if we say that it is not disqualified unless he knew at the time of its mounting, it works out well. And that which we learned in the Mishnah (Parah 2:1) also works out well: "A pregnant [red] heifer — Rabbi Eliezer declares it fit," and it was difficult: Does [Rabbi Eliezer] not hold [that if] a male mounted it, it is disqualified? According to what I have explained, it works out well! Alternatively, he holds like Rabbi Yehudah, who says that specifically if one brought a male upon it [is it disqualified], but if it mounted on its own, it is fit. And Rabbi Yitzchak of Simfon explained that they do not disagree regarding the cow itself, but rather regarding its offspring; and the Rabbis' reason that it is disqualified is as we expound in the Sifrei: "And they shall take for you a cow [parah]" — we require that at the time of taking it be a [full-grown] cow, and Rabbi Eliezer does not hold of that exposition. And the same applies [that] they could disagree where they took a young heifer. And if you ask: One who performs labor with a purification heifer, regarding whom [the Gemara] says in the chapter HaKones (Bava Kamma 56a and there) that he is liable under the laws of Heaven — why is it disqualified? Surely the owners are certainly not amenable! And one can say: [It refers to a case] where he was a partner; alternatively, we do not require the amenability of the owners, only the amenability of the one performing the labor. And if you ask: In the chapter Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 23b), where Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies a heifer purchased from gentiles because he is concerned for bestiality, and [the Gemara] infers: Conclude from this that it is consecrated for the altar, for if it were consecrated for Temple upkeep, why would it be disqualified due to bestiality? Let us say that it is disqualified due to [bearing] a yoke! And one can say: It is clear to [the Gemara] that he does not disqualify [it] on account of a yoke, because it teaches in the latter clause: "And similarly, Rabbi Eliezer would disqualify [them] among other sacrifices"; therefore [the Gemara] says that it is consecrated for the altar, for we exclude an animal subjected to bestiality from the verse "from the cattle." [And see further Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 23b, s.v. "Shema minah."]

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:16:1.hebrew: הא אין עשה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה - וא"ת: דבפ"ב דיבמות (דף כא -) ובפ' כ"ג (סנהדרין דף יט.) לא חשיב אלמנה לכהן גדול אלא לא תעשה גרידא, ואמאי? והא איכא עשה ד"קדושים יהיו"! וי"ל: דלא קאי עשה ד"קדושים יהיו" אלא אמאי דכתיב בההיא פרשה. וא"ת: והא כי אמרינן דאין עשה דוחה את לא תעשה ועשה, ה"מ לא תעשה ועשה השוה בכל, אבל האי דאינו שוה בכל — דחי! כדמוכח פרק שני נזירין (נזיר דף נח:), דאתי עשה דמצורע ודחי לאו ועשה דכהנים. וכן ק' לקמן (בבא מציעא לב.): "יכול אמר לו אביו הטמא כו'", ופריך: "תיפוק ליה דאין עשה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה", הא גבי כהנים שאינו שוה בכל דחי! וי"ל: דעשה דמצורע שאני, דחמיר משום דגדול השלום, כדאמר בפ' שילוח הקן (חולין דף קמא.), דעשה דמצורע הוי דחי לאו ועשה דשילוח הקן אי לאו יתורא ד"שלח תשלח"; אבל עשה דעלמא לא דחי לאו ועשה, אפילו אינו שוה בכל. וזה התירוץ לא יתיישב למאן דשרי מצורע בימי חלוטו בתשמיש המטה פ"ק דמועד קטן (. דף ז:). ולדידיה יש לומר דהכא סמיך על "ותו מי דחינן איסורא מקמי ממונא", ולקמן נמי עדיפא משני, דהוה דחי אפילו לאו ועשה אי לאו קרא, אפי' אי בעלמא לא דחי. ובפ"ב דיבמות (דף כא.) דאמר גבי פלוגתא דר' יוחנן ור"א בביאת כ"ג באלמנה מן הנישואין: "כ"ע לא פליגי דלא פטרה, דאין עשה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה" — וי"ל דחשיב שוה בכל, כיון שהאלמנה עשתה איסור כמו הכהן, דאקרי ביה "לא יקח" — "לא יקחו", אע"ג דאין שוה בכל אלא בכהנים; אבל ההיא דגילוח זקן, שאינו שוה בנשים, נדחי מקמי עשה דמצורע:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:16:1.english: Behold, a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment - And if you ask: in the second chapter of Yevamot (21a) and in the chapter [entitled] Kohen Gadol (Sanhedrin 19a), [the Gemara] considers [the prohibition of] a widow to a High Priest to be only a simple negative commandment — why? Behold, there is the positive commandment of "They shall be holy" [Leviticus 21:6]! And one can answer: the positive commandment of "They shall be holy" refers only to what is written in that section [namely, corpse impurity, and not to forbidden marriages]. And if you ask: when we say that a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment, that applies [only] to a negative commandment and a positive commandment that apply equally to all [Jews], whereas this [prohibition of priest impurity], which does not apply equally to all, should override! As is proven in the chapter [entitled] Shnei Nezirin (Nazir 58b), where the positive commandment of a metzora [to shave] comes and overrides the negative and positive commandments of priests [not to round the corners of the beard]. And similarly it is difficult below (Bava Metzia 32a): "[One] might [think that if] his father said to him, 'Become impure,' etc." — and [the Gemara] asks: "Let it emerge from [the principle] that a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment" — behold, regarding priests, where it does not apply equally to all, it does override! And one can answer: the positive commandment of a metzora is different, as it is more stringent because peace [between husband and wife] is great, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Shiluach HaKen (Chullin 141a), that the positive commandment of a metzora would have overridden the negative and positive commandments of sending away the mother bird from the nest were it not for the superfluous phrase "you shall surely send"; however, a general positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment, even if it does not apply equally to all. However, this resolution will not sit well according to the one who permits a metzora during the days of his confirmed affliction [to engage] in marital relations, in the first chapter of Moed Katan (7b). And according to him, one can say that here [the Gemara] relies on "And furthermore, do we override a prohibition in the face of monetary matters?", and below as well, [the Gemara] gives a stronger answer, that [honoring one's father] would have overridden even a negative commandment and a positive commandment were it not for the verse, even if in general it does not override. And [regarding] the second chapter of Yevamot (21a), where [the Gemara] says concerning the dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar regarding the intercourse of a High Priest with a widow from marriage: "Everyone agrees that it does not exempt [her rival wife], because a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment and a positive commandment" — one can answer that it is considered to apply equally to all, since the widow commits a prohibition just like the priest, as we read [in the verse] "he shall not take [lo yikach]" [as if it were] "they shall not take [lo yikachu]," even though it applies only to priests [and not to all Israel]; whereas that [prohibition] of shaving the beard, which does not apply equally to women, is overridden before the positive commandment of a metzora.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:1:1.hebrew: בתורי דנפיש פסידייהו - ר"ח גרס בתוורי, פירוש: פועלים שמוליכים השוורים לחרישה, ואין מעמיקין המחרישה שלשה טפחים, ואין הזרע נקלט היטב:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:1:1.english: With oxen, whose damage is great - Rabbenu Chananel reads betavri. Explanation: laborers who lead the oxen for plowing, and do not sink the plow three handbreadths [deep], and [thus] the seed is not absorbed well.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:2:1.hebrew: לצורכו ולצורכה מאי - דוקא בשיטוח כסות מבעיא ליה, וכל דדמי ליה, דשמא יניחנה שטוחה יותר מכדי צורכה עד שיתקלקל. אבל בספר, אמרינן דקורא בהן — אף ע"ג דצורכו הוא — כמו צורכה, ולא גזרינן, דליכא למיחש למידי, כיון שקבעו לו זמן: אחד לשלשים יום או אחד לי"ב חדש, ולא ילמוד בו בתחלה, גם לא יקרא וישנה. וכלי נחשת, דתניא לקמן דמשתמש אפי' בחמין, וכלי כסף בצונן — אפי' לצורכו מותר, כיון שעל ידי אותו תשמיש אינו יכול לבא לידי קלקול. ותדע, דאי דוקא לצורך הכלי, מאי פריך: "פקדון מאי עבידתיה גביה"? כיון שהוא שומר, יש לו לעיין שלא יתקלקל, אע"פ שהבעלים אינם אומרים לו להשתמש:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:2:1.english: "If [one spreads it] for his sake and for its sake, what [is the halakha]?" - [The Gemara] raises this dilemma specifically regarding spreading out a garment, and anything similar to it, for perhaps he will leave it spread out longer than is necessary for it until it becomes ruined. However, regarding a scroll, we say that he may read from them — even though it is for his own need — just like for its need, and we do not issue a precautionary decree, for there is nothing to be concerned about, since they established a set time for it: once every thirty days or once every twelve months, and he may not study from it for the first time, nor may he read and review [it]. And [as for] copper vessels — as it is taught in a baraita later on, that one may use [them] even with hot [liquids] — and silver vessels with cold [liquids], it is permitted even for his own need, since through that use it cannot come to ruin. And know [that this is so], for if [it were permitted] only for the need of the vessel, why does [the Gemara] object: "What business does a deposit have with him?" Since he is a guardian, he must take care that it does not become ruined, even though the owners do not tell him to use [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:6:1.hebrew: הכניסה לרבקה ודשה - בתוספת' (דפרה). תני לה גבי פרה אדומה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:6:1.english: One introduced it into a yoke and it threshed - In the Tosefta (Parah), it is taught regarding the red heifer:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:6:2.hebrew: בשביל שתינק ותדוש פסולה - ובסיפא (דתוספתא.) קתני: "לצורכו פסולה, לצורכה כשירה"; ולכך פריך: אלמא לצורכו ולצורכה חשיב כמו צורכו, ואסור. ומשני: דהתם דאורייתא פסולה, כמו בא עלי' זכר, דפסולה מדרב פפא. וא"ת: ואמאי מייתי ההיא דשכן עליה עוף, ואי משום דרב פפא אמר למלתיה עלה — אמאי לא אמר אהך דהכניסה לרבק'? וי"ל: משום דברייתא היא, אבל הך דשכן עליה עוף היא מתניתין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 30a:6:2.english: "So that it will suckle and it will thresh, it is unfit" - And in the latter clause (of the Tosefta) it teaches: "[If he did so] for his sake, it is unfit; for its sake, it is fit"; and therefore [the Gemara] asks: Evidently, [doing something] for his sake and for its sake is considered like [doing it] for his sake [alone], and is forbidden. And [the Gemara] answers: That there, by Torah law it is unfit, just like [the case where] a male mounted it, which is unfit according to Rav Pappa. And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] bring that [teaching] of "a bird rested upon it"? And if [it is] because Rav Pappa stated his teaching regarding it, why did he not state [it] regarding this [case] of "one who introduced it into a yoke"? And one can answer: Because [the latter] is a baraita, whereas that [teaching] of "a bird rested upon it" is a Mishnah.
